findings.proposedIrEvidence: "conditionType": "UNSUPPORTED" applied to conditions whose "description" and "provenance.excerpt" are verbatim, unambiguous quotations of the operative source text (no dangling reference, no missing document, no ambiguity in these particular clauses).
findings.verifierReasoning: The top-level conditions describing the (d)(i) no-cure covenant list and the (d)(ii) residual-covenant/25-day-cure trigger are fully and unambiguously supported by the quoted source text - unlike the genuinely dangling '5.02(g)' cross-reference, there is no missing document, ambiguous target, or unresolved definition affecting these clauses. Labeling them 'UNSUPPORTED' (the same conditionType used for the truly unresolved 5.02(g) carve-out) risks conflating 'this narrative trigger could not be reduced to a structured boolean/threshold expression' with 'this claim lacks source support,' which are very different statements. If a downstream consumer treats 'UNSUPPORTED' as a flag that the condition's factual basis is unverified, it could wrongly discount or exclude an otherwise clear and fully-evidenced Event of Default trigger from compliance analysis. I cannot determine from the evidence given whether 'UNSUPPORTED' in this schema means 'not reducible to formal expression' (a benign modeling limitation) or 'not supported by source' (a mischaracterization), so I flag this as uncertain rather than conclusively material.

findings.sourceEvidence: "Section 6.01. Events of Default. If any of the following events (each an \"Event of Default\") shall occur and be continuing: ... (d)(i) The Borrower shall fail to perform or observe any term, covenant or agreement ... (d)(ii) the Borrower shall fail to perform or observe any other term, covenant or agreement ... then, and in any such event, the Administrative Agent (i) may declare the obligation of each Lender to make the Loan to be terminated ... (ii) may ... declare the Promissory Note, the outstanding principal amount of the Loan ... to be forthwith due and payable ... and (iii) may foreclose upon the Collateral or exercise remedies"
findings.verifierReasoning: Section 6.01(d) is not a neutral, non-operative provision - it is an Event of Default trigger that, once satisfied (subject to any applicable cure period), entitles the Administrative Agent to terminate lending commitments, accelerate the Promissory Note, and foreclose on Collateral. Coding both the action and posture as effectively null/not-applicable could cause a downstream consumer that filters rules by posture (e.g., only surfacing PROHIBITION/OBLIGATION postures as operative constraints) to silently drop this Event of Default trigger from any compliance or capacity analysis, which would understate real default risk. I cannot confirm from the material provided whether the schema simply lacks an EVENT_OF_DEFAULT-style posture/action (making OTHER/N_A the best available fallback) or whether this represents an actual under-classification, so I flag this as uncertain rather than conclusively material.
